claims.statement: Pemvidutide is a synthetic, unacylated GLP-1/glucagon dual receptor agonist in clinical development by Altimmune, Inc., distinct from approved single-target GLP-1 receptor agonists.

Pemvidutide has no FDA-approved indication and is not a marketed drug product; it remains investigational, currently advancing to Phase 3 (PERFORMA trial) for MASH after Phase 2b data, while FDA has granted it Breakthrough Therapy Designation for MASH (based on 24-week IMPACT Phase 2b data) and Fast Track designation for alcohol use disorder (AUD).

claims.statement: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled 12-week Phase 1/2 trial in 94 people with MASLD (BMI >=28.0 kg/m^2, liver fat >=10% by imaging), once-weekly subcutaneous pemvidutide produced dose-dependent reductions in liver fat content (46.6% at 1.2 mg, 68.5% at 1.8 mg, 57.1% at 2.4 mg vs 4.4% for placebo) and body-weight loss peaking at -4.3% at the 1.8 mg dose (p<0.001), and was reported as well tolerated with no severe or serious adverse events.

context.population: adults with MASLD, BMI >=28.0 kg/m^2, liver fat content >=10% by imaging (n=94)
context.doseText: 1.2 mg, 1.8 mg, or 2.4 mg once weekly for 12 weeks (trial protocol; not a use recommendation)

claims.statement: In the Phase 2b IMPACT trial (212 participants with biopsy-confirmed MASH, fibrosis stages F2/F3), 24-week once-weekly subcutaneous pemvidutide produced MASH resolution without worsening fibrosis in 59.1% (1.2 mg) and 52.1% (1.8 mg) of participants versus 19.1% for placebo (p<.0001 both doses); fibrosis improvement without worsening MASH occurred in 31.8% and 34.5% of the 1.2 mg and 1.8 mg groups respectively versus 25.9% for placebo, a difference reported as not statistically significant; mean weight loss was 5.0% (1.2 mg) and 6.2% (1.8 mg) versus 1.0% for placebo (p<.001).

context.population: adults with biopsy-confirmed MASH, fibrosis stage F2/F3, with and without diabetes (n=212)
context.doseText: 1.2 mg or 1.8 mg once weekly for 24 weeks (trial protocol; not a use recommendation)

claims.statement: In the 48-week Phase 2 MOMENTUM obesity trial (topline company-reported results, n=391), gastrointestinal adverse events at the highest dose (2.4 mg weekly) included nausea in 51.5%, vomiting in 27.8%, diarrhea in 18.6%, and constipation in 22.7% of participants, described as mostly mild-to-moderate; drug-related discontinuation rates were 15.5% (2.4 mg) and 16.2% (1.8 mg) versus 2.1% for placebo, and one serious vomiting event was reported at the 2.4 mg dose.

context.population: adults with obesity/overweight and >=1 comorbidity, without diabetes (n=391)
context.doseText: 1.2, 1.8, or 2.4 mg once weekly for 48 weeks (trial protocol; not a use recommendation)

claims.statement: Pemvidutide has no FDA-approved indication, no established human safety profile beyond controlled trials of 12-48 weeks, and no long-term (multi-year) or real-world safety data, yet it is listed for sale by research-chemical vendors (e.g., as an unregistered 'research use only' product) outside any clinical protocol; efficacy and safety for self-administered, non-trial use in the general population -- including for anti-aging, bodybuilding, or general weight-loss marketing framed around it -- are unestablished and outside the scope of the controlled trials summarized here.

context.formulation: research-labeled pemvidutide/ALT-801 sold outside clinical trial protocols

extractedEvidence.quote: shows striking reductions in body weight, liver fat and serum lipids

reviewFlags: misinformation-adjacent: vendor marketing language ('striking reductions') echoes trial topline figures without the population, dose-titration, monitoring, and adverse-event context established in the controlled trials
all published human data to date derive from supervised trials of at most 48 weeks; no chronic self-administration safety data exist

conflicts.summary: MASH-resolution endpoint reached strong statistical significance in the IMPACT Phase 2b trial, but the co-primary/secondary fibrosis-improvement endpoint did not separate significantly from placebo at 24 weeks, which trade-press coverage of the topline data does not consistently emphasize alongside the MASH-resolution headline figures.

The MOMENTUM 48-week obesity trial's efficacy and safety figures are currently available only via sponsor (Altimmune) topline press release; no independent peer-reviewed publication, regulator review, or non-sponsor source for these specific numbers was located this session.
